key_insight: DemoPSD makes policy self-distillation more robust by reducing the harmful effects of overconfident teacher supervision. It uses disagreement between model signals to modulate when and how strongly the student should imitate the teacher.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a core weakness of on-policy self-distillation for LLM reasoning: dense token-level teacher supervision can overfit to in-domain patterns, suppress exploration, and degrade cross-domain generalization.
method: Measures disagreement between teacher and student signals to estimate when supervision is reliable.
Modulates self-distillation strength based on that disagreement, rather than applying uniform dense imitation.
Preserves exploration by avoiding overly restrictive teacher guidance during uncertain or out-of-domain cases.
impact: This matters because it offers a practical way to train reasoning models that generalize better beyond their training distribution. For practitioners, it can improve robustness while keeping the simplicity of self-distillation.
